market_summary: As of 08:32 IST, 20 Nov 2026. Verified facts: on 19 Nov, Nifty 50 closed at 25,514.30 (+1.14%) and Sensex at 83,021.75 (+1.21%); autos led with more than 4% sector gain, banks and consumer durables were firm, while Nifty IT fell 1.11%. NSE-provisional cash flows showed FII net buying of ₹7,411.41 crore and DII net selling of ₹1,356.57 crore. Before the open, GIFT Nifty was 25,352 at 07:57 IST, around 162 points below the prior Nifty close; Wall Street fell 2.0%–2.3% and Asian benchmarks sold off sharply. USD/INR settled at 93.29 on Thursday; Brent was $92.22/bbl and WTI $83.40/bbl in early Friday trade. Post-close filings include an Atul US customs investigation notice, cancellation of Ashoka Buildcon's Saudi project, Paytm's proposed Funding Societies investment, Voltas' compressor JV, a Dilip Buildcon metro LOA, NLC Renewables' proposed IPO filing and Coal India's rare-earth magnet facility LoI. Interpretation: domestic momentum and foreign inflows are supportive, but the overnight global risk-off move and negative GIFT Nifty indication raise near-term gap/volatility risk; the rupee has so far been cushioned by inflows. Portfolio context: the repository's stock-recommendations file lists M&M and SBIN as Watch candidates, not confirmed holdings; no holdings register was found. These are dated snapshots and verified disclosures, not live quotes or investment advice.

global_cues.title: Wall Street extends AI-led selloff; S&P 500 posts sixth consecutive decline
global_cues.detail: Verified: at the 19 Nov US close, the S&P 500 fell 2.0% to 7,175.83, the Dow lost 2.2% to 49,097.06 and the Nasdaq dropped 2.3% to 23,879.20; more than 90% of S&P 500 constituents declined. Anthropic closed its first trading day at $97.17, up 17.1% from its $83 IPO price, but the debut did not reverse broad AI-stock weakness. Interpretation: concerns about AI valuations, data-centre returns, regulation and high interest rates are weighing on global risk appetite. AP's page did not display an exact publication time.
global_cues.source: Associated Press, report on 19 Nov 2026 US market close (publication time not displayed)

global_cues.title: Asian selloff deepens; GIFT Nifty points to a weaker Indian open
global_cues.detail: Verified: Reuters reported at 08:04 IST on 20 Nov that GIFT Nifty stood at 25,352 at 07:57 IST, versus Thursday's Nifty close of 25,514.30. MSCI Asia-Pacific shares were down 2.5%; Japan's Nikkei fell 4.1% and South Korea's KOSPI 4.7%. Interpretation: the futures discount implies a negative opening indication, not a guaranteed spot-market gap or direction for the full session.

global_cues.title: Rupee holds near 93.29 as foreign inflows offset global risk aversion
global_cues.detail: Verified: USD/INR settled at 93.29 on 19 Nov; traders expected a 93.28–93.34 opening range on 20 Nov. Reuters reported that foreign investors bought more than $800 million of Indian shares on Thursday and monthly net purchases had crossed $12 billion; the rupee was up 1.75% in November. Interpretation: strong flows are currently cushioning the currency, but Reuters cautioned that a deeper global sentiment deterioration could overwhelm that support.

global_cues.title: Crude edges higher on Gulf shipping risks but remains set for a weekly decline
global_cues.detail: Verified: Brent rose 0.3% to $92.22/bbl and December WTI rose 0.2% to $83.40/bbl at 01:18 GMT on 20 Nov. Brent was still set for a 3.5% weekly fall and December WTI for a 6% decline. Reuters cited Houthi attacks on Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz as supply-risk factors, against expectations of a global surplus. Interpretation: lower weekly crude prices remain a relative macro cushion for India, while renewed shipping disruption is an upside risk to import costs.

global_cues.title: Potential US rate hike expectations add to dollar and emerging-market pressure
global_cues.detail: Verified: Reuters' 20 Nov pre-market report said firmer odds of a possible US rate hike next month were supporting the dollar. AP also cited high interest rates among the pressures on AI-related equities. Interpretation: higher-for-longer US rates can tighten global financial conditions and create volatility for emerging-market equities, even while current foreign flows into India remain strong.
global_cues.source: Reuters, 20 Nov 2026 02:34 UTC (08:04 IST); Associated Press, 19 Nov US close (publication time not displayed)

intraday.headline: Atul USA receives US CBP investigation notice over alleged antidumping and countervailing-duty evasion
intraday.what_changed: Verified filing: Atul disclosed that its wholly owned subsidiary Atul USA Inc. received a US Customs and Border Protection notice under the EAPA concerning alleged evasion of antidumping and countervailing duties on Chinese 2,4-D and derivatives allegedly transhipped through India. CBP suspended liquidation of covered unliquidated entries entering the US after 11 Aug 2026. Atul said it prima facie denies the allegation and has engaged US counsel; the financial impact is uncertain.
intraday.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the notice introduces regulatory and potential trade-cost uncertainty for the US subsidiary and could affect covered shipments while the investigation proceeds. The allegation is not an adjudicated finding.
intraday.risk: The company has not quantified any duty exposure or financial impact; the scope and duration of the investigation and any further CBP measures are unknown.

intraday.headline: Diriyah Company cancels Ashoka's Saudi hotel construction project valued at ₹846.38 crore for its JV share
intraday.what_changed: Verified filing: the employer notified the joint venture that the Main Construction Works of Diriyah II – Delivery Partner for One Hotel project had been cancelled for internal reasons attributable to the employer. The accepted price for Ashoka's SPV share of work was SAR 351,372,308.67, stated by the company as ₹846.38 crore. Ashoka said it was approaching the employer to understand the reasons and next steps.
intraday.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the cancellation removes a sizeable overseas project from the disclosed execution pipeline. Any recovery, termination compensation or redeployment benefit is not established by this filing.
intraday.risk: The filing does not quantify lost margin, sunk costs, compensation or cash-flow impact; discussions with the employer and any contractual remedies remain unresolved.

intraday.headline: Paytm Singapore proposes up to ₹200 crore investment in Funding Societies units and a technology partnership
intraday.what_changed: Verified filing: Paytm Singapore, a step-down wholly owned subsidiary, approved a proposed investment of up to ₹200 crore in Funding Societies subsidiaries. The initial approximately ₹162 crore would acquire a 19.1% stake in CardUp; up to approximately ₹38 crore may go to an affiliate. Paytm will also provide payments and lending technology to CardUp for technology fees and revenue share. The proposed investment is subject to confirmatory due diligence, corporate approvals, definitive documents and regulatory approvals.
intraday.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the partnership extends Paytm's partner-operated international payments strategy and could add fee/revenue-share opportunities, but the economics and contribution to group earnings are not yet established.
intraday.risk: The investment is proposed rather than completed; diligence, approvals, final documentation, execution and the returns from CardUp remain uncertain.
intraday.source: One 97 Communications Regulation 30 filing, 19 Nov 2026 18:22 IST

swing.headline: Voltas executes 50:50 Atomberg JV agreement for room air-conditioner compressors
swing.what_changed: Verified filing: Voltas executed a joint venture agreement with Atomberg Innovation for development, manufacture and commercialisation of room AC compressors and related parts in India. Voltas will acquire 50% of Atomberg Airtech on closing; the parties will each hold 50%, while Voltas can nominate four directors and Atomberg one. Each party's maximum funding commitment is ₹100 crore, subject to the agreement's conditions precedent.
swing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the venture could give Voltas greater control over an upstream compressor capability and support longer-term product/supply-chain strategy. The filing does not yet establish production capacity, launch timing or earnings contribution.
swing.risk: Closing conditions, plant location, capacity, commercialisation schedule, customer demand, unit economics and actual funding deployment remain unspecified.

swing.headline: Receives ₹419.47 crore Letter of Acceptance for Gurugram Metro depot-cum-workshop
swing.what_changed: Verified filing: Dilip Buildcon received a Letter of Acceptance from Gurugram Metro Rail Limited for construction of a depot-cum-workshop, including civil, architectural and E&M works, at Sector 33, Gurugram. The stated project cost is ₹419.47 crore including GST, with a 21-month completion period.
swing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the LOA adds a defined domestic metro project and execution visibility. Revenue and margin realisation will depend on mobilisation, milestone execution and working-capital discipline.
swing.risk: The filing does not disclose project margin, payment milestones or mobilisation requirements; execution delays, cost overruns and working-capital absorption remain risks.

investing.headline: NLC India Renewables files DRHP for proposed IPO with fresh issue up to ₹3,300 crore and OFS up to 10 crore shares
investing.what_changed: Verified filing: NLC India disclosed that its wholly owned subsidiary NLC India Renewables Limited filed a draft red herring prospectus with SEBI, BSE and NSE on 19 Nov. The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares aggregating up to ₹33,000 million (₹3,300 crore) and an offer for sale of up to 10,00,00,000 shares held by NLC India. The offer remains subject to approvals, market conditions and other considerations.
investing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: a separate listing could provide a valuation reference for the renewables subsidiary and the fresh issue could fund its growth; the OFS component would monetise part of the parent's holding rather than raise proceeds for the subsidiary.
investing.risk: The DRHP is not an approval or final offer; pricing, final issue size, valuation, dilution, use of fresh-issue proceeds and listing timing are not settled.
investing.source: NLC India Regulation 30 filing, 19 Nov 2026 15:32:29 IST

investing.headline: Coal India-led consortium receives LoI for 1,200 TPA rare-earth permanent-magnet facility
investing.what_changed: Verified filing: the Ministry of Heavy Industries issued a Letter of Intent dated 19 Nov for a sintered NdFeB rare-earth permanent-magnet manufacturing facility. Coal India is lead member of a consortium with NFTDC and is described in the filing as the L2 bidder. The stated capacity is 1,200 tonnes per annum, with a seven-year schedule comprising two years of pre-construction and five years of operations; no monetary contract value is stated.
investing.why_it_matters: Interpretation: the proposal offers long-term diversification into strategic-material manufacturing and a potential role in domestic magnet supply chains, but it is a long-gestation project rather than a near-term earnings catalyst.
investing.risk: The filing gives no monetary consideration, capex, funding structure, expected returns or commercial start date; the L2-bidder status and SPV/project execution are important conditions to monitor.
